# Research report 1 of 2

I couldn't find the official result page, odds or forecasts dated on or before the 2026-09-11 cutoff, so the evidence below is thin. Nothing published by the cutoff settles the question. Several sources I came across were published after the cutoff, so I left them all out of the report.

## 1. Resolution source
- The criteria give no URL. The official source is LaLiga's match record, with Flashscore and then Sofascore as fallbacks. LaLiga's Betis results page is [here](https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/clubs/real-betis/results). I found no pre-match status for this game there dated by the cutoff.
- Betis are at home. Sources disagree on the ground: the Wikipedia 2026-27 season page and Goal's ticketing page say Estadio de La Cartuja, while FotMob and TUDN say Benito Villamarín. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026%E2%80%9327_Real_Betis_season), [Goal tickets](https://www.goal.com/en-us/tickets-travel/team/real-betis-tickets/A~bltf21ce63ff717778e)

## 2. Current status
- As of 2026-09-11 the match has not been played, and nothing settles or nearly settles the question.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
These come from search-result summaries of ESPN, LaLiga and Sofascore results lists. I did not check each result on a primary page.
- 2026-09-08: Lille 2-3 Betis, Champions League (away win). [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/soccer/team/results/_/id/244/real-betis)
- 2026-09-04: Betis 1-0 Real Madrid at La Cartuja, goal by Parrott in the 81st minute. Wikipedia's Real Madrid season page calls this Madrid's first league defeat. [LaLiga](https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/match/temporada-2026-2027-laliga-ea-sports-real-betis-real-madrid-4), [Wikipedia RM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026%E2%80%9327_Real_Madrid_CF_season)
- 2026-08-29: Levante 5-2 Betis (away loss). [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/soccer/team/results/_/id/244/real-betis)
- 2026-08-25: Valencia 0-1 Betis (away win). [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/soccer/team/results/_/id/244/real-betis)
- 2026-08-21: Betis 1-0 Real Sociedad (home win). [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/soccer/team/results/_/id/244/real-betis)
- Getafe: Bordalás is coach. They are said to have opened September with draws against Levante and Celta Vigo, but I couldn't confirm the exact dates or their full early-season table by the cutoff. One source says Getafe finished 7th in 2025-26. [Sportsmole](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/getafe/preview/getafe-vs-malaga-prediction-team-news-lineups_605397.html), [Trivela](https://trivela.com.br/espanha/la-liga/o-getafe-recorre-novamente-a-pepe-bordalas-para-tentar-evitar-o-rebaixamento-em-la-liga/)
- Players named for each side in sources: for Betis, Álvaro Valles, Natan, Isco, Abde and Parrott. For Getafe, David Soria, Mario Martín, Iván Azón and Satriano. I found no injury news dated by the cutoff.

## 4. Base rates
- Head to head: in their last home meeting with Getafe (2025-26) Betis won 4-0, and Betis also won 4-0 at Getafe late in 2025. [comuniate](https://www.comuniate.com/noticias/37955/betis-getafe-previa-alineaciones-probables-y-consejos-fantasy-jornada-6-de-laliga), [ESPN Deportes](https://espndeportes.espn.com/futbol/espana/nota/_/id/16109550/betis-getafe-laliga-equipo-fecha-hora-y-tv-en-vivo)

- 2026-27 so far: Betis have won 2 of 2 league home games, both 1-0. Getafe under Bordalás are usually low-scoring, defensive and hard to beat.
- I couldn't find a published home win rate for Betis against mid- or lower-table sides. A rough general reference is that LaLiga home teams win about 45-50% of games, and home favourites against weaker sides usually win more often than that. This is general background, not a figure from a source I checked.
